configuration_reports.label: yes
controls_available: Visible two-line dispatch order and five-second task clock for each of five rounds.
gate_tag: click the instructed moving stage token while its center is inside the white gate.
sync_hold: hold the instructed stage token and release it on the amber cue after both needles enter the notch.
vector_flick: drag from the instructed stage token in the required direction while its pointer faces the requested heading.
relay_pair: tap the two instructed stage tokens on the stage in the requested order.
shutter_drop: drag the instructed cargo token into the instructed live bay while its shutter is open.
autonomous_processes: Every round advances autonomously from roundStartedAt: the visible countdown changes continuously and the round fails at 5000 ms without a successful dispatch.
gate_tag: stage tokens move at the generated target speed 88 px/s (with 10 px sinusoidal vertical motion) and the target's membership in the 66px half-width gate changes.
sync_hold: two needles move with elapsed task time; the cue begins at a generated 1420–1570 ms start and lasts 460 ms, with 300 ms timing tolerance.
vector_flick: each token pointer rotates continuously; difficulty 1 uses 44° orientation tolerance and 34px minimum direct travel.
relay_pair: token positions are static during the pair, but the five-second round clock continues while the two ordered taps are pending.
shutter_drop: the target bay's shutter opens/closes autonomously for 1450 ms in a 2300 ms cycle; the visible aperture and open state change while the 78px bay remains the target.
grouped_control_modes: D=direct_tag: every direct moving-token tag action across all gate_tag rounds, seeds, and attempts.
D=direct_hold: every direct token hold/release across all sync_hold rounds, seeds, and attempts.
D=direct_flick: every direct pointer drag across all vector_flick rounds, seeds, and attempts.
D=direct_tap: every direct ordered stage-token tap across all relay_pair rounds, seeds, and attempts.
D=direct_drag: every direct cargo-to-bay drag across all shutter_drop rounds, seeds, and attempts.

clause_i.reason: For the common witness D=direct_drag, take histories at the same task time before the bay action with identical I_t and no prior bay choice. The generator samples target_bay_index independently for each deck, so different seeds require different bay IDs and visible bay coordinates; q(I_t) is therefore identical where the delayed-optimal action is not. The fixed target-bay phase does not remove this cross-seed target identity ambiguity.

clause_ii.reason: g uses the bounded W_t^600 window (six chronological frames), the two-line instruction, and the visible stage/proxy geometry. The target color identifies the correct bay; consecutive frames expose the target bay's changing open state and aperture, allowing direct_drag from the visible cargo to the visible bay center to be delivered at t+Delta. Cargo selection itself can be prepared before the timed bay action in simplified mode.

clause_iii.reason: At t≈1580 ms, the target bay is at the center of its open interval. With no new action for Delta=800 ms, it is closed (the target phase is beyond the 1450 ms open interval), so the same bay drag/click a loses its outcome value; the next opening begins at about 3155 ms, before the 5000 ms round ends, so success remains possible. The strict loss is the autonomous shutter/aperture state change, not merely less deadline time.

configuration_reports.common_visible_process: Common witness for full: in every shutter_drop round, the generator makes one randomly selected target bay visible and centers its cyclic opening near 1580 ms; the browser continuously renders its open/closed state and aperture. Over Delta=800 ms from the open center, the target shutter closes, making the direct cargo drag invalid at the same bay while the next opening (about 3155 ms) remains available. The same six-frame, 600 ms visible window supplies the target identity and the shutter trajectory used to choose the delayed action.

pre_run.reason: The generator always emits gate_tag, sync_hold, vector_flick, relay_pair, and shutter_drop, and the grader requires all five dispatches. Gate, hold, flick, and drop each require an outcome-affecting action at a changing or time-specific state during the round; a solution that sends no outcome-affecting actions throughout the autonomous outcome phases cannot complete a generated deck. Thus no generated instance qualifies for a pre-run solution in this mode; no percentage is asserted.
